exposure: Prenatal stress (measured using the Prenatal Distress Questionnaire and serum cortisol levels)
outcome: Birth experience (measured using the Childbirth Experience Questionnaire)
cohort: 398 pregnant women who gave birth at the Punta de Europa University Hospital in Algeciras (Spain) between September 2021 and August 2023
finding: Higher levels of prenatal stress were associated with higher blood cortisol levels, an increased risk of caesarean section, and lower Apgar scores at 1 minute.
mod_finding: Women with higher prenatal stress had an increased risk of having a caesarean section.
